cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to walk you through an example of a two-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 講師：這支影片會帶你看一個雙因子 ANOVA 的例子。

cues.en: This is going to give you more experience interpreting experiments in the context of ANOVA's and interpreting the ANOVA table and the degrees of freedom
cues.zh: 讓你更熟悉在 ANOVA 脈絡下解讀實驗，以及解讀 ANOVA 表與自由度，

cues.en: and also more experience with interpreting and working with interaction terms and main effects.
cues.zh: 也累積更多解讀與處理交互作用項、主效應的經驗。

cues.en: Okay, so here is the question.
cues.zh: 問題如下。

cues.en: Are girls worse than math than boys?
cues.zh: 女生的數學比男生差嗎？

cues.en: So do you think that there is something about girls that makes them worse in math than other technical subjects than boys?
cues.zh: 你認為女生有什麼特質，讓她們在數學或其他技術科目上，比男生差？

cues.en: Or do you think that this is just a stereotype that we think that girls should be worse than boys?
cues.zh: 還是認為這只是刻板印象，讓我們以為女生應該比男生差？

cues.en: Well, this is what our experiment is going to test.
cues.zh: 這就是實驗要檢驗的。

cues.en: So we are going to test whether girls differ from boys in STEM and non-STEM subjects.
cues.zh: 檢驗女生與男生在 STEM 與非 STEM 科目上，是否不同。

cues.en: STEM stands for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
cues.zh: STEM 代表科學、科技、工程與數學。

cues.en: So basically a bunch of technical topics and non stem would be like, humanities and arts and other non-technical subjects.
cues.zh: 基本上是各種技術主題，非 STEM 則是人文、藝術等非技術科目。

cues.en: So the way that we are going to set up this experiment is by creating three different classrooms.
cues.zh: 實驗會安排三種不同教室。

cues.en: One classroom has only boys and no girls.
cues.zh: 一間只有男生，沒有女生。

cues.en: One classroom has only girls and no boys, and one classroom is mixed.
cues.zh: 一間只有女生，沒有男生，另一間則混合。

cues.en: There are boys and there are girls in the same classroom.
cues.zh: 同一間教室裡有男生也有女生。

cues.en: So for this mixed classroom, we're actually going to separate our group into the boys because we wanna look at the exam scores
cues.zh: 混合教室還要把男生另外分組，因為想分開查看

cues.en: from the boys separately from the girls.
cues.zh: 男生與女生的考試分數。

cues.en: So that gives us our four different groups, even though we have three classrooms here.
cues.zh: 因此，雖然有三間教室，卻得到四個不同群組。

cues.en: Okay, so these are the levels, the groups within the factor class, gender, we could just call this class.
cues.zh: 這些是班級性別因子內的水準、群組，也可以直接叫班級因子。

cues.en: And then we have the factor subject, which is the topic of the studies, and that is math or history.
cues.zh: 另外有科目因子，也就是學習的主題，分為數學或歷史。

cues.en: And then at the end of the two month period, we have an exam, and that's our dependent variable, the exam scores.
cues.zh: 兩個月後進行考試，考試分數就是依變數。

cues.en: Okay, so the idea is we have three classes of 20 students each, and they're studying the same material from the same teacher so that the, any random effect of teacher
cues.zh: 概念是，三班各有 20 位學生，由同一位老師教相同教材，因此教師的任何隨機效應，

cues.en: is held constant here.
cues.zh: 在這裡保持固定。

cues.en: Okay, now again, as with all the other examples in this course, I actually made up the numbers for the data.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，就像課程其他例子，這些資料的數字都是我編的。

cues.en: But in this case, the main conclusion and the inspiration for this project are actually based on real reach research.
cues.zh: 但這次的主要結論與專案靈感，其實基於真實研究。

cues.en: So the conclusions that we can draw here are actually supported by real experiments and real data, although I'm making up the numbers in this particular video.
cues.zh: 因此，這裡可以得到的結論，受到真實實驗與資料支持，雖然這支影片的數字是編的。

cues.en: All right, so here we see the ANOVA table.
cues.zh: 這裡是 ANOVA 表。

cues.en: So we have the main facts here, the factor group and the factor subject.
cues.zh: 有群組因子與科目因子的主效應。

cues.en: And we have the interaction between the group, the class and the subject.
cues.zh: 有群組、班級與科目之間的交互作用。

cues.en: And then the within group variance also sometimes called the error and the total, okay?
cues.zh: 接著是組內變異，也稱為誤差，以及總計。

cues.en: So you can see this table is empty and the degrees of freedom column is in this like bluish, greenish, cyanish color.
cues.zh: 表格是空的，自由度欄用偏藍、偏綠、青色顯示。

cues.en: Now, what I would like you to do in a moment is pause the video and fill out that column.
cues.zh: 稍後希望你暫停影片，填完這一欄。

cues.en: So just based on the information I provided in the previous slide, you should be able to compute the degrees of freedom for all of these different these five different cells.
cues.zh: 只根據上一張投影片的資訊，應該就能計算這五個不同格子的自由度。

cues.en: Now, if you want to hint, I'm going to show you the formulas for computing the degrees of freedom in a moment.
cues.zh: 如果需要提示，稍後會展示計算自由度的公式。

cues.en: So if you don't wanna hint, if you want to pause the video and do this without a hint, then now is your chance, pause the video.
cues.zh: 不想看提示、想自行完成，現在就可以暫停。

cues.en: Okay, and here comes the hint.
cues.zh: 提示來了。

cues.en: So here's the hint, these are the formulas for computing the degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 這些是計算自由度的公式。

cues.en: So you still have to do a bit of work to get the solution, but this should help you get started if you are struggling a little bit.
cues.zh: 仍然需要自己算出答案，但如果有點卡住，這應該有助於開始。

cues.en: Okay, now pause the video. All right, how did it go?
cues.zh: 暫停影片。好，做得如何？

cues.en: Did you figure it out?
cues.zh: 想出來了嗎？

cues.en: So here is the actual answer, and then I'm not really gonna talk about this too much, but you can pause the video if you need more time to check your answers against these numbers.
cues.zh: 這是真正答案，我就不多解釋；如果需要更多時間核對，可以暫停影片。

cues.en: Okay, and then these are the P-values here.
cues.zh: 這裡是 P 值。

cues.en: So we find that there is a statistically significant interaction between group and subject.
cues.zh: 可以看到，群組與科目之間有統計顯著的交互作用。

cues.en: That's this term here.
cues.zh: 就是這一項。

cues.en: This interaction makes the main effect of subject, which is this P-value here, difficult to interpret without subsequent visualization and possible postdoc comparison tests.
cues.zh: 這讓科目主效應，也就是這個 P 值，在沒有進一步視覺化與可能的事後比較檢定前，很難解讀。

cues.en: So there's no main effect of of group that's already kind of interesting.
cues.zh: 群組沒有主效應，這已經有點有趣。

cues.en: There is a main effect of the subject and there's a significant interaction between them.
cues.zh: 科目有主效應，兩者之間有顯著交互作用。

cues.en: Now, one thing I would like to point out here is in my text here in actual research papers, when people are reporting the statistics from an ANOVA,
cues.zh: 想指出，實際研究論文報告 ANOVA 統計結果時，

cues.en: they usually want to typographically separate the factors and the interaction terms, the ANOVA terms from the rest of the text.
cues.zh: 通常會用字體排版，把因子與交互作用項，也就是 ANOVA 項，與其他文字區隔。

cues.en: So there's a couple of different ways that people do that.
cues.zh: 有幾種不同方式。

cues.en: There's no like one standard way to separate the names of the factors from the rest of the text, but I'm showing you here three different possibilities.
cues.zh: 要把因子名稱與其他文字區分，沒有單一標準方式，但這裡展示三種可能的做法。

cues.en: One is to capitalize them.
cues.zh: 一種是首字母大寫。

cues.en: So I'm capitalizing group to indicate that it is a factor.
cues.zh: 把 Group 首字母大寫，表示它是一個因子。

cues.en: Another way is to italicize.
cues.zh: 另一種是斜體。

cues.en: So here I'm italicizing subject to indicate that that's a factor.
cues.zh: 這裡用斜體 subject，表示是因子。

cues.en: And here I'm bolding the factor term.
cues.zh: 這裡則把因子名稱加粗。

cues.en: Now in practice, when you are writing about the results of your ANOVA, you don't wanna mix these different forms.
cues.zh: 實際撰寫 ANOVA 結果時，不要混用不同形式。

cues.en: You wanna pick one of these three, but I just showed you all three in the same paragraph so that it's just, yeah, just to show you the different options.
cues.zh: 從三種中選一種；這裡只是在同一段示範全部三種，讓你看到不同選項。

cues.en: But the main point is somehow you want to separate out the names of these statistical factors.
cues.zh: 主要重點是，以某種方式區隔這些統計因子的名稱。

cues.en: So they're easy to see.
cues.zh: 讓它們容易辨識。

cues.en: Other times you might see people write out the factor names in all capital letters.
cues.zh: 有時也會看到因子名稱全部大寫。

cues.en: That is personally my least favorite option because when I see writing in all caps, I just think that someone is yelling at me and it makes me a little anxious,
cues.zh: 這是我個人最不喜歡的選項，因為看到全大寫，就像有人對我大吼，讓我有點焦慮，

cues.en: like maybe I did something wrong by just their yelling group and subject at me anyway.
cues.zh: 好像我做錯事，他們在對我大喊 GROUP 與 SUBJECT。

cues.en: Okay, so something is different somewhere and we need to visualize the data in order to determine what is driving this interaction
cues.zh: 總之，某處有差異，需要把資料視覺化，判定是什麼造成交互作用，

cues.en: and whether it's safe to interpret this main effect given that the interaction term is statistically significant.
cues.zh: 以及在交互作用顯著時，是否仍能安心解讀主效應。

cues.en: Okay, so here I have the data graph here.
cues.zh: 這裡是資料圖。

cues.en: So the first thing that we can look for is the main effect.
cues.zh: 首先查看主效應。

cues.en: Now in this case it seems pretty clear that we can interpret the main effect of the study subject, and that's because the average of all the history scores
cues.zh: 這裡似乎很清楚，科目主效應可以解讀，因為全部歷史分數的平均，

cues.en: is higher than the average of all of the math scores.
cues.zh: 高於全部數學分數的平均。

cues.en: So when we ignore group, then we see that people are just scoring higher on the history exam and lower on the math exam.
cues.zh: 忽略群組，會看到歷史考試分數就是較高，數學較低。

cues.en: So this main effect here actually can be safely interpreted even in the presence of this interaction term, but we wouldn't have known that without visualizing the results.
cues.zh: 所以即使有交互作用，這個主效應仍可以安心解讀；但不把結果畫出來，就不會知道。

cues.en: So now we need to look at the interaction term.
cues.zh: 接著看交互作用項。

cues.en: And the interaction term is telling us that something between these two-factors, which is the colored bars, that's the group and the the two groups of bars,
cues.zh: 交互作用告訴我們，這兩個因子，也就是彩色長條代表群組，而兩組長條

cues.en: which is the subject, is different.
cues.zh: 代表科目，兩者之間有些東西不同。

cues.en: Now, when you look at this, you can see that the difference is really driven by the girls in the mixed classroom who are scoring lower on the math exam.
cues.zh: 可以看到，差異主要來自混合教室的女生，她們的數學分數較低。

cues.en: And then you can compare that to the orange bar, which is the math exams of the classroom that only had girls and no boys.
cues.zh: 可以與橘色長條比較，那是只有女生、沒有男生的教室，其數學考試分數。

cues.en: So this is what's driving the interaction here, and you don't see that effect for history.
cues.zh: 這就是交互作用的來源，歷史科目看不到這個效果。

cues.en: So this is the sort of data that we could say is consistent with the idea that there are some stereotypes against girls doing well in math when the boys are present.
cues.zh: 這種資料，可以說符合這樣的想法：男生在場時，存在不利於女生數學表現的刻板印象。

cues.en: So somehow, the presence of boys is activating these stereotypes and then the girls are somehow doing more poorly than they would have if they were in their own classroom.
cues.zh: 男生在場以某種方式啟動這些刻板印象，讓女生比只在女生教室中，表現得更差。

cues.en: Now, as I mentioned, this is probably like the fifth time that I'm saying this already.
cues.zh: 如前所述，大概已經說第五次了。

cues.en: This is actually consistent with what educational research has shown.
cues.zh: 這其實符合教育研究的發現。

cues.en: So this isn't so far from the truth, although I did just make up these bars here.
cues.zh: 所以並非與真實世界相差很遠，雖然這裡的長條是我編的。

cues.en: Okay, what I want to show you now is multiple different ways of highlighting or visualizing the same exact data set.
cues.zh: 現在要展示，同一份資料集可以用多種方式凸顯、視覺化。

cues.en: This is something that I already introduced you to in the section on visualization when I was talking about grouping bar plots together.
cues.zh: 這在資料視覺化單元談群組長條圖時，已經介紹過。

cues.en: So what I'm going to do now is show you the same exact results.
cues.zh: 現在展示完全相同的結果。

cues.en: I didn't change any of the heights of these bars, I'm just grouping them in different ways.
cues.zh: 沒有改變任何長條高度，只是用不同方式分組。

cues.en: So here we have boys only, boys mixed, girls only, girls mixed and then the what's grouped together is the math versus history.
cues.zh: 這裡是全男班男生、混合班男生、全女班女生、混合班女生，再把數學與歷史分成一組。

cues.en: So then you see that, the history scores are higher, higher, higher, higher.
cues.zh: 可以看到，歷史分數在每一組都較高。

cues.en: And here, yeah, I mean it's the same data as in the previous side.
cues.zh: 這與上一張投影片是同一份資料。

cues.en: Now you can decide for yourself what you think your brain is automatically figuring out when you look at this.
cues.zh: 你可以自行判斷，看圖時，大腦會自動注意到什麼。

cues.en: But when I look at the data organized like this, what I see actually is the difference between math and history.
cues.zh: 但我看到這種排列，先注意到的其實是數學與歷史的差異。

cues.en: That seems to be the most prominent difference.
cues.zh: 那似乎是最突出的差異。

cues.en: And it takes me a little bit longer to figure out that this is an unusual data point because really in the entire dataset, this is the most striking data point.
cues.zh: 要多花一點時間，才發現這是一個不尋常的資料點；其實它是整份資料中最醒目的點。

cues.en: But that seems harder, it takes me longer to come to that conclusion here and here with this original way of showing the data that is much more visually apparent,
cues.zh: 這種畫法讓我花更久才得出結論，而原本這種呈現方式，視覺上就明顯得多，

cues.en: your brain immediately goes to this difference here.
cues.zh: 大腦立刻注意到這裡的差異。

cues.en: And this overall main effect of subject is a little bit less pronounced in this way of visualization.
cues.zh: 科目整體主效應，在這種視覺化中就比較不突出。

cues.en: But I would say that's fine because that seems to be much less interesting.
cues.zh: 但我覺得沒關係，因為那個似乎比較不有趣。

cues.en: That is not such an interesting finding in this study that people score higher on history exam than on math exams in general.
cues.zh: 這個研究中，人們歷史考試分數通常比數學高，並不是特別有趣的發現。

cues.en: Okay, so for this particular message, I would say this is the better way of visualizing.
cues.zh: 所以對這個特定訊息而言，我認為這是更好的視覺化方式。

cues.en: On the other hand, you could imagine changing the experiment or changing the question so that this is the more appropriate way to visualize.
cues.zh: 另一方面，也可以改變實驗或研究問題，讓另一種方式更適合。

cues.en: Let's say we wanted to know if math tests are harder than exams in other subjects.
cues.zh: 假設想知道，數學考試是否比其他科目更難。

cues.en: So then, if that's your question, then this seems like a good way to visualize the data because we are seeing that everyone seems to be doing worse on their math exam
cues.zh: 如果是這個問題，這樣畫就很好，因為可以看到，所有人數學考試的表現，似乎都比

cues.en: compared to the history exam.
cues.zh: 歷史考試差。

cues.en: So in this video I showed you another example of a two-factor ANOVA.
cues.zh: 這支影片又展示了一個雙因子 ANOVA 的例子。

cues.en: You also saw the importance of visualizing an interaction term in order to be able to determine whether a significant main effect is interpretable.
cues.zh: 也看到把交互作用項視覺化，對判定顯著主效應能否解讀有多重要。

cues.en: And finally, I reinforce the idea that it's really important how you visualize data because that's going to affect how people interpret your results.
cues.zh: 最後，再次強調資料如何視覺化非常重要，因為會影響人們如何解讀結果。
